{{Short description|Operator in analysis and probability theory}}
The '''{{Lang|fr|carré du champ operator|italic=no}}''' (French for ''square of a field'' operator) is a [[bilinear map|bilinear]], [[symmetric map|symmetric]] operator from [[Mathematical analysis|analysis]] and [[probability theory]]. The {{Lang|fr|carré du champ operator|italic=no}} measures how far an [[C0-semigroup#Infinitesimal generator|infinitesimal generator]] is from being a [[Derivation (differential algebra)|derivation]].<ref name="Ledoux1">{{cite journal|first=Michel |last=Ledoux |title=The geometry of Markov diffusion generators |journal=Annales de la Faculté des Sciences de Toulouse: Mathématiques|series=Série 6 |volume=9 |number=2 |date=2000 |page=312 |doi=10.5802/afst.962 |url=http://www.numdam.org/item/AFST_2000_6_9_2_305_0/|doi-access=free |hdl=20.500.11850/146400 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

The operator was introduced in 1969<ref>{{cite journal|first=Hiroshi |last=Kunita |title=Absolute continuity of Markov processes and generators |journal=Nagoya Mathematical Journal |volume=36 |date=1969 |pages=1–26 |doi=10.1017/S0027763000013106 |s2cid=118693611 |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/nagoya-mathematical-journal/volume-36/issue-none/Absolute-continuity-of-Markov-processes-and-generators/nmj/1118797793.full|doi-access=free }}</ref> by {{ill|Hiroshi Kunita|qid=Q114965633|short=yes}} and independently discovered in 1976<ref name="roth">{{cite journal|first=Jean-Pierre |last=Roth |title=Opérateurs dissipatifs et semi-groupes dans les espaces de fonctions continues |journal=Annales de l'Institut Fourier |volume=26 |number=4 |date=1976 |pages=1–97 |doi=10.5802/aif.632 |url=http://www.numdam.org/item/AIF_1976__26_4_1_0/|doi-access=free }}</ref> by [[Jean-Pierre Roth (mathematician)|Jean-Pierre Roth]] in his doctoral thesis.

The name ''"carré du champ"'' comes from [[electrostatics]].

==Carré du champ operator for a Markov semigroup==
Let <math>(X,\mathcal{E},\mu)</math> be a [[σ-finite measure|σ-finite]] [[measure space]], <math>\{P_t\}_{t\geq 0}</math> a [[Markov semigroup]] of non-negative operators on <math>L^2(X,\mu)</math>, <math>A</math> the [[Markov operator#Infinitesimal generator of the semigroup|infinitesimal generator]] of <math>\{P_t\}_{t\geq 0}</math> and <math>\mathcal{A}</math> the algebra of functions in <math>\mathcal{D}(A)</math>, i.e. a [[vector space]] such that for all <math>f,g\in \mathcal{A}</math> also <math>fg\in \mathcal{A}</math>.

===Carré du champ operator===
The '''{{Lang|fr|carré du champ operator|italic=no}}''' of a Markovian semigroup <math>\{P_t\}_{t\geq 0}</math> is the operator <math>\Gamma:\mathcal{A}\times \mathcal{A}\to\mathbb{R}</math> defined (following [[Paul-André Meyer|P. A. Meyer]]) as
:<math>\Gamma(f,g)=\frac{1}{2}\left(A(fg)-fA(g)-gA(f)\right)</math>
for all <math>f,g \in \mathcal{A}</math>.<ref>{{cite journal|first=Michel |last=Ledoux |title=The geometry of Markov diffusion generators |journal=Annales de la Faculté des Sciences de Toulouse: Mathématiques|series=Série 6 |volume=9 |number=2 |date=2000 |pages=305–366 |doi=10.5802/afst.962 |url=http://www.numdam.org/item/AFST_2000_6_9_2_305_0/|doi-access=free |hdl=20.500.11850/146400 |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite encyclopedia |first=Paul-André|last=Meyer |title=L'Operateur carré du champ |publisher=Springer |encyclopedia=Séminaire de Probabilités X Université de Strasbourg |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics |volume=511 |place=Berlin, Heidelberg |date=1976 |pages=142–161 |lang=fr |doi=10.1007/BFb0101102|isbn=978-3-540-07681-0 }}</ref>

===Properties===
From the definition, it follows that<ref name="Ledoux1" />
:<math>\Gamma(f,g)=\lim\limits_{t\to 0}\frac{1}{2t}\left(P_t(fg)-P_tfP_tg\right).</math>

For <math>f\in\mathcal{A}</math> we have <math>P_t(f^2)\geq (P_tf)^2</math> and thus <math>A(f^2)\geq 2 fAf</math> and
:<math>\Gamma(f):=\Gamma(f,f)\geq 0,\quad \forall f\in\mathcal{A}</math>
therefore the {{Lang|fr|carré du champ operator|italic=no}} is positive.

The domain is
:<math>\mathcal{D}(A):=\left\{f \in L^2(X,\mu) ;\;\lim\limits_{t\downarrow 0}\frac{P_t f-f}{t}\text{ exists and is in } L^2(X,\mu)\right\}.</math>

===Remarks===
*The definition in Roth's thesis is slightly different.<ref name="roth" />
